title: The creation options of the 19 schemas are not specified
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 29, 38, 39 and 41; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md section R4; WP B-PLT-DB-01 story line RWB-PLT-NF06-DB
section: 3 Preconditions; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: The sources fix one schema and one login per service and the 19 names, and they fix nothing about how a schema is created: the owner beyond the rule that the login owns it, the encoding and collation, the tablespace, the ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES set, the search_path of each login, and whether the ACE DBA account creates all 19 in one run or each service team creates its own. A build team can create a schema that satisfies the ownership rule and still differ from the next environment in encoding, collation, tablespace or default privileges, and the boundary that slide 29 relies on would then depend on how each run was made.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 29 gives the rule 'each service has one database login that owns its schema' and names no encoding, collation, tablespace, default privilege or search_path; slide 39 decision 2 gives 19 schemas and 19 logins and no creation option; slide 41 gives the 19 schema names and the note 'schema rwb_<name> in the ACE database with its own login' and no option; Template and Rules section R4 gives the schema name shape only; no source read names an encoding, a collation, a tablespace, a default privilege or a search_path.
proposed: Fix in RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and in the ACE DBA standard: each schema owned by its own login, UTF8 with the server default collation, the default tablespace, ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES granted to the owning login only, search_path set to the service's own schema, and all 19 created once by the ACE DBA account in one transaction.

title: The environments that receive the 19 schemas in wave 0 and the role that runs the script there are not specified
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 29 and 38; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md sections R5.6 and R5.7; WP B-PLT-DB-01 story line RWB-PLT-NF06-DB
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 10 Authority; 13 Solution plan
description: Wave 0 lists the 19 schemas and logins as a platform item built once, and the programme runs four environments, but no source states which environments receive the schemas in wave 0, whether all four are created at once or UAT and PROD wait for the first service of their wave, which role runs the script in an environment, or which change record each run needs. The story therefore cannot say from the documents alone where it is done, and a run in a production environment without a stated role would leave the change unauditable.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 38 lists '19 schemas + logins' under wave 0 'Platform once' and names no environment; slide 29 describes one ACE PostgreSQL server without naming an environment; Template and Rules section R5.6 puts platform and NF in wave 0 and names no environment; section R5.7 rule 6 makes the platform stories Day-1 work and states no environment; no source read states the environment set of wave 0, the role that runs a schema script or the change record of a run.
proposed: Fix in RWB-PLT-NF03-OPS and in this story: DEV and SIT receive the 19 schemas in wave 0 by this story, UAT and PROD receive them by the same idempotent script at the release of the first service of each wave, the ACE DBA role runs the script, and each run carries its own change record.

title: Whether the service login or a separate migrator login applies the migrations is not specified
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 29; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md section R5.5 DP-15; WP B-PLT-DB-01 story lines RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and RWB-PLT-N011-DB
description: Slide 29 states that the login owns its schema and that each service runs its own Flyway migrations, which reads both as the owning login applying them and as a separate migrator applying them on the owner's behalf; no source names a migrator login. The same Work Package carries a second story, RWB-PLT-N011-DB 'PgBouncer pools, migrator role and grant check', which implies a separate migrator without stating the split. A build team cannot tell which identity its migrations run as, and a grant of DDL to the owning login would be either required or redundant depending on the answer.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 29 rules text: 'each service has one database login that owns its schema and has no grant on any other schema ... Each service runs its own Flyway migrations'; slide 39 decision 2 gives 'no cross-schema access' and no migrator; Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-15 gives the per-service sequence in the service's own schema and no identity; no source read names a migrator login or states that the owning login applies the migrations itself.
proposed: State in RWB-PLT-N011-DB that the migrations are applied by a per-service migrator login granted on its own service's schema only, that the owning login keeps ownership and that this story grants no DDL beyond ownership.

title: Pool mode, default pool size, connection cap per login, idle and connection timeouts and the server-side reserve are not specified
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 29, 39 and 41; Template and Rules v1 sections R4 and R5.5 DP-02; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md NFR-020, NFR-021, NFR-052 and NFR-053; WP B-PLT-DB-01 story line RWB-PLT-N011-DB
section: 3 Preconditions; 11 Data (the 19 pools); 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: Architecture v5 fixes the shape of the protection and one number inside it: slide 29 says each login goes through its own PgBouncer pool with a connection cap and a statement timeout, slide 39 decision 2 adds a connection budget per service, and slide 11 fixes a 5 s statement timeout for the SQL view standard. No source read fixes the pool mode (session, transaction or statement), the default pool size, the connection cap of any of the 19 logins, the idle timeout, the connection timeout, the server-side reserve, the maximum client connections of the pool process, or the name of a pool entry. The story can state and test the rule and the 5 s timeout, but a platform engineer cannot configure a pool that protects the server until the ACE DBA sets the numbers, and a cap that is too high protects nothing while one too low throttles a service in wave 1.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 29: 'ACE POSTGRESQL SERVER / PgBouncer pool and connection cap per login', 'Capped connections: PgBouncer pool per login protects ACE' and 'each login goes through its own PgBouncer pool with a connection cap and statement timeout'; no cap, pool size, mode or timeout value on the slide. Arch v5 slide 39 decision 2: 'connection budget per service' with no number. Arch v5 slide 11 standards table, SQL view row: transport 'PostgreSQL TLS; read-only login', identity 'One login: rwb_source_data', timeout column '5 s statement timeout', the only numeric value in any source. NFR-020 and NFR-021 state the availability targets and no connection value.
proposed: The ACE DBA publishes, per login, a connection cap, a pool size, the pool mode, the idle and connection timeouts and the server-side reserve before the first release, the platform holds every one of them as a configuration value and never in code, and the 5 s statement timeout of Arch v5 slide 11 stands unchanged on every pool.

title: Migrator login naming, its number, the role that creates it and how its credential is held are not specified
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 29 and 39; Template and Rules v1 section R4 and section R5.5 DP-02 and DP-15; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md NFR-052; WP B-PLT-DB-01 story line RWB-PLT-N011-DB
section: 3 Preconditions; 11 Data (the 19 migrator logins); 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: The target rule is one service login that owns its schema and runs its own Flyway migrations, and the monolith ran its migrations as a single recovery migration account. No source read says whether the account that runs a service's migrations is the service login itself, a second login per service, or one shared migration account; it gives no name pattern for a migrator login, no list of the DDL privileges it holds inside its own schema, no statement of whether it owns the objects it creates or creates them as the schema owner, and no rule for how its credential is held and rotated. The story needs a migrator login to state AC3 and AC4, so the shape is assumed and recorded, but a platform engineer cannot create the roles from the documents alone.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 29: 'each service has one database login that owns its schema and has no grant on any other schema ... Each service runs its own Flyway migrations', one login and one migration path, with no second login named. Arch v5 slide 39 decision 2 names the owners (ACE team, DBA) and no role name. Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-15 names the per-service Flyway sequence and no account. NFR-052 requires the credential in the key store and no source gives an object path for it.
proposed: One migrator login per service, named after its schema with the suffix _migrator, owning nothing and a member of no service login, holding DDL on its own schema only, created once per service by the ACE DBA with its credential held in the key store as a reference.

title: Whether the per-login cap is delivered by the managed PgBouncer of the Azure Database for PostgreSQL service or by a PgBouncer deployment the platform runs is not specified
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 29 and 39; Template and Rules v1 section R9; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md NFR-020 and NFR-021; WP B-PLT-DB-01 story line RWB-PLT-N011-DB
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow step 2; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: Architecture v5 names PgBouncer as the mechanism and the ACE PostgreSQL server as 'Azure Database for PostgreSQL' (slide 29 notes), but no source read says whether the pool is the managed PgBouncer feature of that service or a PgBouncer deployment the platform operates in front of it, and no source says how a per-login cap is expressed in the chosen product: one pool per login, one database or user entry per login, or a per-role setting. The difference decides where the configuration lives, whether the platform can set a statement timeout per login, how the pool statistics are exposed for RWB-PLT-N005-OPS, and whether the platform or the database service owns a restart.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 29 title 'ACE POSTGRESQL SERVER / PgBouncer pool and connection cap per login' and notes 'Physical: the ACE PostgreSQL server (Azure Database for PostgreSQL)' with 'each login goes through its own PgBouncer pool with a connection cap and statement timeout'; Arch v5 slide 39 decision 2 names the server and no product shape. No source names the managed feature, a PgBouncer version or a deployment.
proposed: The platform runs PgBouncer itself with one database or user entry per login so that the cap and the statement timeout are per login and the statistics are readable on the platform metrics path, and the ACE DBA confirms the deployment shape before wave 1.

title: Where the grant check runs, what it publishes and how long the result is kept are not specified
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 29 ('Checked in every build'); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-15 and section R7.2 s16; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md NFR-054; WP B-PLT-DB-01 story line RWB-PLT-N011-DB
section: 4 Flow steps 6 and 7; 5 Exception paths; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: Architecture v5 says only that a boundary test fails every build on a cross-schema reference, and NFR-054 says the pipeline blocks a change that carries a secret, personal data or an unapproved dependency. No source read says which pipeline runs the grant check of the 19 logins (the platform pipeline, one service pipeline per repository, or both), what the check publishes besides its exit code, whether one result per login is attached to the run or written to the catalogue, how long a result is kept for the audit trail, and which role reads it. The story can fix a blocking stage and one result per login per run, but the DevOps lead cannot wire or retain it from the documents alone.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 29: 'Checked in every build / boundary test fails on a cross-schema reference', with no stage, tool, artefact or retention. NFR-054 states the blocking rule and no pipeline mechanism. Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-15 places the migration lint and drift gate with RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and says nothing of a stage that checks grants across the 19 logins; no source gives a result format or a retention period.
proposed: The grant check is one blocking stage of the platform pipeline beside the migration lint and drift gate of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, publishes one result per login per run attached to the run, and is kept with the pipeline history for the audit period agreed with internal audit.
